US-119-HR10937.title: PROTECT 340B Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10937.description: To amend title XXVII of the Public Health Service Act to ensure the equitable treatment of covered entities and pharmacies participating in the 340B drug discount program, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10937.aiSummary: This bill would change rules for the 340B drug discount program so covered health providers and their contract pharmacies must be treated like other providers and pharmacies by health plans, insurers, and pharmacy benefit managers. It would bar lower pay, extra fees, limits on networks, and other different terms based on 340B status, and it would allow penalties of up to $5,000 per violation per day for pharmacy benefit managers. The bill would also extend these rules to some Medicare plans, set up data checks to help stop duplicate Medicaid rebates, and block federal funds from being used to carry out a 2020 order that limited what covered entities charge patients for 340B drugs.

US-119-HR10915.title: Common-Sense Cloud Security Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10915.description: To require the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop new standards, methodologies, and recommendations with respect to the cybersecurity of cloud-based infrastructure, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10915.aiSummary: The bill would direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology to study cloud security and publish new rules and advice for cloud-based systems. It would also create a voluntary cloud security certification program for private companies, with public listings of certifications and tiered levels. The bill would affect cloud service providers, federal agencies, and owners and operators of critical infrastructure.

US-119-HR10838.title: Honesty in Government Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10838.description: To extend the statute of limitations for making false statements to Congress, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10838.aiSummary: The bill would give a 10-year time limit for bringing cases over false statements, hiding facts, or fraudulent claims made in matters tied to Congress. It would apply to work done by Congress, such as committee investigations, reviews, and oversight matters. The change would apply only to offenses committed on or after the date it takes effect.

US-119-HR10816.title: DORIE Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10816.description: To amend title 10, United States Code, to prohibit the naming of Department of Defense assets for sitting Presidents, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10816.aiSummary: The bill would bar the Defense Department from naming or renaming facilities, aircraft, ships, or other assets after a sitting president. It would also block Defense Department funds from being used for that purpose. Any Defense asset already named for the current president would have to go back to its earlier name when the law takes effect.

US-119-HR10717.title: Wigs for Warriors Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10717.description: To amend title 10, United States Code, to provide wigs to TRICARE beneficiaries with alopecia, including alopecia caused by chemotherapy, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10717.aiSummary: The bill would change military health law to provide wigs to TRICARE beneficiaries who have alopecia, including hair loss caused by chemotherapy. It would affect people covered by TRICARE who have this kind of hair loss. The bill was introduced in the House and sent to the House Armed Services Committee on October 1, 2026.

US-119-S5677.title: Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5677.description: A bill to establish the Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area to conserve, protect, and promote the economic benefits of the natural, cultural, and recreational resources of the Upper and Middle Texas Gulf Coast as a unit of the National Park System.
US-119-S5677.aiSummary: The bill would create the Lone Star Coastal National Recreation Area as part of the National Park System to protect and promote the natural, cultural, and recreation resources of the Upper and Middle Texas Gulf Coast. It would allow the Interior Secretary to work with Texas, local groups, landowners, and others to manage the area, use voluntary land deals, and set up a partnership and management plan. It also would let the federal government help fund some projects, with federal money matched by at least three non-federal dollars for every federal dollar.

US-119-S5633.title: STEP Improvement Act of 2026

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5633.description: A bill to amend the Small Business Act to reauthorize the State Trade Expansion Program of the Small Business Administration, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5633.aiSummary: The bill would reauthorize the Small Business Administration’s State Trade Expansion Program, which helps states support small businesses that want to sell abroad. It would change the grant process, including application timing, simpler forms, more public program information, and an annual survey of states that got grants. It would also set new rules for how grant money is divided among states, territories, and commonwealths, and limit how much a grant can drop from year to year.

US-119-S5556.title: Accessible Ukraine Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5556.description: A bill to require all construction and renovation projects in Ukraine receiving funding from the United States to comply with accessibility standards that are substantively equivalent to the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, the Architectural Barriers Act of 1968, and related regulations.
US-119-S5556.aiSummary: The bill would require U.S.-funded construction and renovation projects in Ukraine to meet accessibility standards for people with disabilities, similar to U.S. rules under the Americans with Disabilities Act and the Architectural Barriers Act. It would cover projects funded through U.S. agencies and funds named in the bill, with some exceptions for normal upkeep and temporary emergency work. The Secretary of State could waive the rule in the national interest, and the bill would also create an accessibility working group and require yearly reports to Congress.

US-119-S5512.title: Stop Wall Street Looting Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5512.description: A bill to subject certain private funds to joint and several liability with respect to the liabilities of firms acquired and controlled by those funds, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5512.aiSummary: The bill would make some private investment funds responsible for certain debts and liabilities of companies they buy and control. It would also add rules on worker pay, bankruptcy priorities, taxes, investor disclosures, and risky debt deals for the funds and the companies they affect.

US-119-S5039.title: License to Drill Act
US-119-S5039.summary:
License to Drill Act

This bill extends through FY2037 the Bureau of Land Management’s (BLM’s) authority to collect oil and gas permit processing fees. For each new permit application, BLM collects a fee that is transferred to the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund. (Under current law, the fees are authorized through FY2026.)
US-119-S5039.summarySource: Congressional Research Service summary (Introduced in Senate, 2026-07-21)

actions.text: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 659.
Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Reported by Senator Lee without amendment. Without written report.
Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Ordered to be reported without amendment favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5039.aiSummary: The bill would extend until fiscal year 2037 the Bureau of Land Management’s power to collect fees for processing new oil and gas permit applications. Those fees go into the BLM Permit Processing Improvement Fund. It would affect people and companies that apply for new oil and gas permits on federal land.

US-119-SJRES216.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval of the proposed foreign military sale to the Government of Saudi Arabia of certain defense articles and services.

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-SJRES216.aiSummary: This joint resolution would block a proposed U.S. military sale to Saudi Arabia. The sale includes thousands of bomb guidance kits, bombs, and related parts and support services. It would affect the U.S. government and the Government of Saudi Arabia.

US-119-HR9849.title: Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources, and in addition to the Committee on the Budget, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House
Sponsor introductory remarks on measure. (CR E729)

US-119-HR9849.description: To authorize Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. to establish a commemorative work in the District of Columbia and its environs, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9849.aiSummary: The bill would let Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. build a memorial on federal land in Washington, D.C., and nearby areas to honor the original Tuskegee Airmen from World War II. It would require the project to follow federal rules for memorials and would bar the use of federal money for it. Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. would be responsible for raising and paying for the memorial.

US-119-HCONRES114.title: Recognizing the significance of equal pay and the disparity in wages paid to men and to Black women.

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.
Submitted in House

US-119-HCONRES114.aiSummary: This concurrent resolution would recognize the pay gap faced by Black women and its effect on women, families, and the country. It also would reaffirm Congress’s support for equal pay for equal work and for narrowing the gender wage gap. A concurrent resolution is a formal statement from both chambers of Congress.

US-119-S1596.title: Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge Act
US-119-S1596.summary:
Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge Act

This act renames the Anahuac National Wildlife Refuge located in Anahuac, Texas, as the Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge.

The act provides statutory authority for Executive Order 14229 , which also renamed the refuge as the Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge.

US-119-HR2215.title: Salem Maritime National Historical Park Redesignation and Boundary Study Act
US-119-HR2215.summary:
Salem Maritime National Historical Park Redesignation and Boundary Study Act

This act redesignates the Salem Maritime National Historic Site in Massachusetts as the Salem Maritime National Historical Park. In addition, the act directs the Department of the Interior to conduct and report on a boundary study. The study must evaluate the suitability and feasibility of including in the National Park System, as part of the Salem Maritime National Historical Park, sites and resources in the study area associated with its maritime history, coastal defenses, and military history.
